name: India
summary: Spectrum is auctioned per Licensed Service Area (22 LSAs); Jio, Airtel and Vi are the private operators, and state-owned BSNL/MTNL gets administrative reservations. The last auctions were in 2022 (5G) and June 2024; TRAI recommended the next auction in Feb 2026.

operators.name: Jio
operators.notes: Acquired RCom's 800/1800 MHz spectrum by trading (2017–2019).

operators.name: Airtel
operators.legal: Bharti Airtel Ltd / Bharti Hexacom Ltd
operators.notes: Bharti Hexacom holds the licences in Rajasthan and North East.

operators.name: Vi
operators.notes: Formed by the Vodafone India–Idea Cellular merger (Aug 2018); rebranded Vi in 2020.

operators.name: BSNL / MTNL
operators.legal: Bharat Sanchar Nigam Ltd; Mahanagar Telephone Nigam Ltd
operators.notes: State-owned. MTNL covers Delhi and Mumbai; BSNL the other 20 LSAs. BSNL gets administrative (non-auction) reservations in 700 MHz, 3300 MHz and 26 GHz for 4G/5G.

operators.name: Adani Data Networks
operators.notes: Won 400 MHz of 26 GHz in 2022 for captive use; agreed in April 2025 to transfer it to Airtel.

operators.name: Reliance Communications
operators.legal: Reliance Communications Ltd / Reliance Telecom Ltd
operators.notes: Ceased mobile service in 2017–2019; in insolvency (IBC). Residual spectrum still recorded against it.

operators.name: Aircel
operators.notes: Shut down in 2018; in insolvency (IBC). Residual spectrum still recorded against it.

notes: Licensing is regional: every band except the pan-India 700 MHz frequency plan is licensed per LSA, with different amounts in each. Holdings are shown as the sum over the 22 LSAs divided by 22 (paired amounts per direction), with the pattern given in each basis. Per-LSA amounts come from a crowd-sourced LSA-by-LSA chart (onlytech.com Google Sheet) and were checked against the regulator's per-band totals of assigned and vacant spectrum in TRAI's Sept 2025 consultation paper: they match exactly for 800, 900 (with BSNL's reservation added), 2100, 2300, 2500, 3300 and 26 GHz; 1800 MHz differs by 9.15 MHz summed across LSAs.
The crowd chart puts BSNL's 3300 MHz holding at 350 MHz; TRAI says 70 MHz is reserved for BSNL 5G in every LSA (1540 MHz). The TRAI figure is used.
Reliance Communications and Aircel (both in insolvency) still have spectrum recorded against them. It is not in use, and TRAI (Feb 2026) recommended that DoT take it back and auction it.

Auctions: 2022 (600 MHz unsold; 700/3300/26 GHz sold in all LSAs; Adani Data Networks entered with 26 GHz); June 2024 (about 141 MHz sold, mainly Airtel, no bids for 3300 MHz or 26 GHz). TRAI's 24 Feb 2026 recommendations cover 600 MHz to 26 GHz; DoT was still reviewing them in the last sources found (spring 2026).
Some administratively assigned 1800 MHz spectrum is released as service licences expire in 2026–2027 (TRAI Annex II); which operator-LSAs are affected by 2026-09-28 was not compiled.

Non-IMT users in IMT bands are excluded from holdings: defence in 800/1800 MHz, Government in 2100 MHz (19 MHz per LSA), Indian Railways GSM-R in 900 MHz. In 700 MHz the TRAI table's government users are drawn because the plan is national.
missing: Adani→Airtel 26 GHz trade (April 2025): closing not confirmed from a primary source; kept under Adani.
No auction between the June 2024 auction and 2026-09-28 was found, but results after about April 2026 could not be checked because the web-search budget ran out.
Per-LSA frequency positions (block edges) for 800–2500 MHz, 3300 MHz and 26 GHz: not compiled; averages only.
Per-operator figures rest on a crowd-sourced chart (matched to TRAI band totals), not on a DoT operator-by-LSA holdings register.
Licence expiry dates per LSA, and the 2026–2027 expiry of administratively assigned spectrum: not compiled.
